title: What is a VoIP number? A guide for small businesses
summary: Learn what a VoIP number is, how it works, and why small businesses are switching from landlines to flexible, affordable VoIP phone numbers.
body_markdown:
A voice over internet protocol (VoIP) number — sometimes called a virtual phone number or VoIP phone number — is a telephone number that works over the internet instead of a traditional phone line. Unlike a landline tied to a physical location, a VoIP number can ring on a desk phone, a laptop, or a mobile device, all at once. For small businesses, that flexibility makes a real difference: your business number travels with you, your team stays reachable wherever they work, and you skip the hardware costs and long-term contracts that often come with legacy systems.

## How a VoIP number works


When you make a call using a VoIP number, your voice is converted into digital data packets and sent over the internet — the same way an email or a video stream travels. On the other end, those packets are reassembled and converted back into audio. The whole process happens in milliseconds.


What makes this powerful for businesses is that the VoIP number itself isn't tied to a wire or a location. It lives in the cloud. That means you can assign it to any device, ring multiple phones simultaneously, set up call routing rules, and manage everything from an admin dashboard — no on-site technician required. For a small business owner who's also the IT department, that simplicity matters.


## VoIP number vs. landline vs. mobile: what's the difference?


Not all phone numbers work the same way. Here's how a VoIP number stacks up against the alternatives many small businesses are currently using.


Feature VoIP number Landline Mobile number


**Works over the internet** ✓ ✗ Via cellular


**Use on any device** ✓ ✗ Phone only


**Keep one number across devices** ✓ ✗ ✗


**Built-in AI features** ✓ ✗ ✗


**Easy to scale** ✓ ✗ Limited


**No extra hardware needed** ✓ ✗ ✓


**Call routing and shared lines** ✓ Limited ✗


Landlines offer reliability, but they lock you to a desk and require physical infrastructure. Mobile numbers are flexible, but using a personal cell number for business creates a blurry line and doesn't give you professional features like call routing or shared lines. A business VoIP number gives you the best of both: professional-grade features with the flexibility to work anywhere.


## Types of VoIP numbers


Not all VoIP phone numbers are the same. Understanding the different types helps you pick the right fit for your business.


### Fixed VoIP numbers


A fixed VoIP number is tied to a registered physical address. This is the most common type for businesses because it supports emergency services (enhanced 911, or E911) — meaning when someone dials 911, their location can be identified. Fixed numbers also tend to carry more credibility with customers.


### Non-fixed VoIP numbers


A non-fixed VoIP number isn't tied to a physical location. These are common with remote teams or businesses that don't have a single office address. They offer flexibility but may have limitations with E911 support depending on your provider and configuration.


### Local VoIP numbers


A local VoIP number carries a familiar area code, which can build trust with local customers. You can often get a local number in any market, even if your team is distributed across the country.


### Toll-free VoIP numbers


Toll-free numbers (800, 888, 877, etc.) project a national presence and let customers call you at no charge to them. Many VoIP providers offer toll-free numbers as part of their plans.


## Key benefits of a VoIP number for small businesses


Small businesses switch to VoIP numbers for a few clear reasons.


**Lower costs.** Traditional phone systems require hardware, installation, and per-line fees. VoIP eliminates most of that. With many VoIP providers, you pay a predictable monthly fee per user, with no hidden charges for SMS or standard 911 support.


**Flexibility.** Your team can take calls from a laptop, a mobile app, or a desk phone — all using the same business number. That's particularly useful for hybrid or remote teams who need to stay reachable without giving out personal cell numbers.


**Professional features.** VoIP numbers come with call routing, shared lines, call queues, auto-attendants, and voicemail — features that used to require an expensive private branch exchange (PBX) setup. With a cloud-based system, you get all of this out of the box.


**AI that handles the busywork.** Modern VoIP platforms can automatically generate call summaries, prioritize voicemails, and surface next steps after every conversation — freeing your team to focus on the work that actually moves your business forward.


**Number portability.** You can transfer your existing business phone number to a VoIP system, so customers never notice the switch.

## Is a VoIP number right for your business?


A VoIP number may be a strong fit if any of these sound familiar:


- Your current phone system is tied to a physical office, but your team works from multiple locations
- You're paying for a legacy private branch exchange (PBX) that's difficult to manage or expensive to maintain
- Customers are reaching your personal cell, and you want a dedicated business number
- You're opening a new location and don't want to deal with new phone line installation
- You need features like call routing, shared lines, or voicemail — without a big up-front investment


If your business is growing and your phone system is holding you back, a VoIP number is usually the clearest path forward.


## How to get a VoIP number in 3 steps


Getting a VoIP phone number is faster than most people expect.


1. **Choose a VoIP provider.** Look for a provider that offers the features your team needs — call routing, mobile app, AI call summaries, and integration with your other tools. Consider whether you want a provider that bundles phone with meetings and chat, so your team isn't jumping between apps.
2. **Pick your number.** You can transfer your existing business phone number to your new VoIP system (this is called porting), or you can get a new local, toll-free, or vanity number. Most providers walk you through this during setup.
3. **Configure your system and go.** Set up call routing, assign numbers to team members, and install the app on your devices. With a cloud-based system, this typically takes minutes — not days.

## Frequently asked questions about VoIP numbers


### What is a VoIP number?


A VoIP number is a phone number that works over the internet rather than a traditional phone line. It can be used on any device — a desktop app, a mobile phone, or a desk phone — and comes with professional calling features like call routing, shared lines, and voicemail. Because it lives in the cloud, it's not tied to a physical location.


### Can I keep my existing phone number with VoIP?


Yes. Most VoIP providers, including Zoom Phone, support number porting — the process of transferring your existing business phone number to your new VoIP system. You can bring your number over, so customers won't notice any change.


### Is a VoIP number the same as a virtual phone number?


The terms are often used interchangeably, but there's a subtle difference. All VoIP numbers are virtual in the sense that they aren't tied to a physical wire. "Virtual phone number" is a broader term that can also refer to numbers that forward calls to another line. A VoIP phone number specifically routes calls over the internet using VoIP technology.


### What's the difference between a fixed and non-fixed VoIP number?


A fixed VoIP number is tied to a registered physical address and supports E911, making it the standard choice for businesses with an office location. A non-fixed VoIP number isn't linked to a specific address, which offers flexibility for remote teams but may have limitations with emergency services depending on your provider and setup.
